# NOTES: Project Gutenberg text, *Morley Ashton: A Story of the Sea* by James Grant (3 vols, 1876, Tinsley Bros). Text given in full; these notes compress it.

## Environment/meta (not part of the book)
- Working dir: /home/shivank/personal/mm-bench-evals/tools-claude-cli/work; git repo; linux.
- CLAUDE.md-style rules: be extremely concise, sacrifice grammar; use Horizon proxy for any LLM calls; Linear via GraphQL only; Smoldata CLI only for Smoldata tasks. User email shivank@bespokelabs.ai (not to be repeated).
- Task: compact the book text into reusable notes; no commentary, no answering questions.

## VOL. I (Chapters I–XXVII)
Front matter: "Morley Ashton: A Story of the Sea," by James Grant (author of "The Romance of War," "Fairer than a Fairy"). Tinsley Brothers, London 1876. Printer: Charles Dickens and Evans, Crystal Palace Press.

**Ch I "The Blind Goddess"**: Late May/late spring evening. Morley Ashton (thin, sallow, tanned, short hair, moustache, soldier-like; grey tweed suit; courier-bag) returns to Acton-Rennel after 3 years on the Bonny River (West Africa; camwood, ivory, palm oil for Liverpool house; fever). Landed at Mersey the night before. Walks from Acton station on London & North-Western line. Passes Norman church (Lykegate, yews), alehouse, lane where Dick Turpin robbed the rector. Meets Ethel Basset (his fiancée 4 years; ~20 yrs old) at Cherrywood Hill/ lane; she carries parasol. Split sixpence motif; lock of hair; "Love is a sting of joy, but a heartache for ever!" Morley's friend Tom Bartelot (Liverpool) nursed him on brig at Foche Point. Ethel reveals father's (Mr. Scriven Basset) losses; family sailing to Isle of France (Mauritius) where Basset appointed one of three judges of supreme civil & criminal court. Morley: "Oh, what fatality is this!"

**Ch II "Laurel Lodge"**: Morley was only son of failed Liverpool merchant. Ethel described (features regular, pensive, sings, rides, billiards, archery). Mother died (Ethel housekeeper young). Scriven Basset: ex-barrister London, rich marriage, retired to Acton-Rennel 18 yrs; easy-tempered, elegant tastes. Laurel Lodge: villa of laurels, sycamores, 17th-c. old part, Elizabethan porch, Basset arms (three bars wavy, two unicorns). Interior: Sèvres, Dresden, Rembrandt tables, buhl clock, Burmese idols. Basset drinking port, walnuts. Mentions Shakespeare (Fortune quote). Captain Cramply Hawkshaw introduced as "son of old Tom Hawkshaw, of Lincoln's Inn," staying months; going to Mauritius. Basset's Mauritius promise to Morley is empty. Morley sees a strange nugget-like ring with green stone on Ethel's finger.

**Ch III "Cramply Hawkshaw"**: Rose Basset (18, brown-haired hoyden, merry). Hawkshaw: under middle height, tough; sinister eyes; tarboosh-like smoking cap, Spanish sash, no waistcoat, bowie-knives, six-shooters; claims Partizan Rangers (Texas), "captain"; digger/Spanish/Yankee slang. Basset's wife died 3 years earlier, buried under old yew at Acton church. Hawkshaw sneers at Morley; Morley: "Hawkshaw ... Poco e poco..." Morley thinks rival.

**Ch IV "Rivalry"**: Late April. Walks of Acton Chase (Shamble-oak, Acton Mere, Cherrywood Hill, Norman cross, Acton Chine—chasm, ~400 ft). Hawkshaw boasts: lasso story (Barranca Secca, Mexico, Vera Cruz–Puebla de Perote road). Zuares Barradas (half-Mexican, half-Spanish sailor; deserted ship at San Diego; met at Feather River diggings). Zuares takes Katarina's crucifix/bracelets; old woman (Zuares' mother, veiled, carried duros) decapitated by Zuares; amulet of cow's horn reveals "Mia madre!" Hawkshaw takes the thirty silver duros. Brother Pedro Barradas attacked; Hawkshaw lassoed him, dragged 200 yds. Lucy Page, Jack Page (Lucy's brother), Mr. Page family neighbors.

**Ch V "Suspicion"**: Story continues: Barradas brothers had kidnapped a widow's son near Laguna d'Alvarado (ear sent; boy and padre stabbed by Pedro). Hawkshaw's lasso and dragging of Pedro. Hawkshaw cites Goethe. Morley: "D---- his impudence!" Hawkshaw's ring: found in Mexico at battle by Juarez; "from Santa Anna's daughter" later. Ethel gives Morley the ring to return; Morley pockets it. Morley resolves to guard against Hawkshaw. Ethel: "Hawkshaw...proposed to her 5 years ago at 17" (Hawkshaw sees ring as Ethel's; Morley doubts).

**Ch VI "For the Last Time"**: Hermione (500 tons, London), captain John Phillips; sailing from London Docks in 14 days. Servant Nance (Nurse) Folgate. Morley writes agents to get cabin passage. Last Sunday in Acton church; curate; pew. Ethel's tears; Morley's parents buried at Denbigh hills. Farewell visits to village, mother's grave (Ethel gathers daisies into packet of English earth). Morley goes to Acton station to telegraph about berth.

**Ch VII "The Rejection"**: May evening; Hawkshaw proposes to Ethel in Acton Chase near Shamble-oak. Ethel: "I cannot love you." Hawkshaw's intemperance (Amontillado, champagne, brandy). Ethel: "since I was seventeen...loved another." Ethel leaves at Pages' gate; Jack Page to see her home. Hawkshaw: "Curse her! ... crush her proud heart... like a rotten castano." Sees Morley on way to seashore.

**Ch VIII "Morley and Hawkshaw"**: Evening; Hawkshaw offers cigars. Morley: telegram to Acton-Rennel announced cabin passage on Hermione; letter posted to Laurel Lodge. Hawkshaw had burned that letter from Basset's post-bag. Morley: "I'm to go with our dear friends... Bassets." Walk to Acton Chine. Scenery described; Edgar's Dover quote. Moon rising red. Morley draws out ring to return. Hawkshaw creeps near, "pale, damp, distorted." "About an hour after this, the captain was seen...alone." Final line: "He was alone!"

**Ch IX "Alarm"**: Night; Hawkshaw back at Laurel Lodge. Says he parted from Morley at path to chine; Morley had telegram good news. Basset, Ethel, Rose alarmed. Search: Basset, Hawkshaw, gardener. Found Morley's grey wide-awake hat (name in lining), kid glove, cigar-case, two half-smoked cigars; ruts/grass torn at edge. Gardener: "he would be drowned". Morley presumed drowned; London detectives suspect foul play; Hawkshaw helps search.

**Ch X "Poor Ethel"**: Ethel grieves; Morley's room, miniature of Ethel, travelling bag, telescope, flask. Ethel suspects Hawkshaw (his shaking hand, champagne rattling teeth, Barradas story). Ethel finds Hawkshaw wears his own ring again. Basset alarmed; leave ~10th day; Hawkshaw goes in Morley's place on Hermione.

**Ch XI "Darkness made Light"**: Morley and Hawkshaw at Chine (chimes of Acton church). Hawkshaw rants about Texas, Sierras. Ring returned: Hawkshaw claims Santa Anna's daughter gift. "Awfully spooney upon Miss Basset." Morley: "Stand back, sir." Hawkshaw strikes, pushes Morley over cliff. Morley: "Save me—Ethel!" Clutches turf, falls. Hawkshaw walks home, bathes hands in runnel; moon rising.

**Ch XII "On Board the good Ship 'Hermione,' of London"**: Ten days in London; embarkation; towed by paddle-tug Garibaldi; Gravesend, Sheerness, Deal, Isle of Wight, Devon coast fades. Captain John Phillips (bluff, ruddy, little). Mates: Samuel Quail (senior), Mr. Foster (second), Adrian Manfredi (Italian third). Surgeon Leslie Heriot (Scot, F.R.C.S.E.). Boatswain etc. Crew mixed (Yankees, West Indians, Mexicans); Pedro Barradas on yard-arm; Hawkshaw dreads him.

**Ch XIII "Acton Chine"**: Morley on ledge ~35–40 ft below verge; guano & moss broke fall. Night; moon; sea birds. Morning: sees ships; fisher-boat missed him; steamers; waves shirt signal. Evening ~6pm: square-rigged ship (Princess? no—Hermione's rescuer is Princess, later) comes near; Morley waves white shirt.

**Ch XIV "The Rescue"**: Ship lies to; boat with six men; rope with bottle of brandy-grog and note ("Take a pull at the bottle..."). Morley hauled up; passed out. Mate Morrison (Scot) and crew; ship is Bartelot's Princess of London (300 tons), bound Rio. Storm; they put to sea.

**Ch XV "An Old Shipmate"**: Morley wakes; Tom Bartelot. Princess (not Rattler). Bartelot: "Rattler" was broken up. Wreck chart. Morley explains Hawkshaw. Songs ("Who is always drinking yet always dry"). Morley's despair; Bartelot's cheer.

**Ch XVI "Under the Tropic of Capricorn"**: Morrison (Scottish mate; Bill Morrison), Noah Gawthrop (old salt; tattoo of ship Haurora). Gale; storms; Prussian ship declines (later). Morley's loneliness; Morrison's theories; Tropic of Capricorn.

**Ch XVII "Second Hearing"**: Morrison's tale of "second hearing": voice "God help me, mother!" heard by mother across North Sea. Morrison's tale of being marooned in boat by Magnus Sigurdson (Scrabster), Harold Trasnaldson; lots; rescued by Danish galliot Thorson.

**Ch XVIII "Rio de Janeiro"**: Morley seeks passage to Mauritius; Cabo Frio; Rio harbour; Castle of Santa Cruz; Sugarloaf; Thetis frigate wreck 1830. Morley's love for Ethel; eventual letter.

**Ch XIX "Ethel amid the Atlantic Isles"**: Hermione: sparrows' nest destroyed (Pedro suspected); foremast carried away; Teguise, Lanzarote (Canaries) refit; Hawkshaw avoids Barradas (shaves beard). Shark incident; Dr Heriot; Manfredi; porpoises; wreck; Psalm.

**Ch XX "Moonlight on the Sea"**: Captain Phillips jokes about Rose & Heriot. Manfredi tells Ethel sad past (Italy).

**Ch XXI "The Story of a Brave Boy"**: Manfredi's brother Attilio (Pistoja, 1850; Kossuth; Count Rudolf de Veinrich; Padre Marraccini; shot by 12 Croats; Adrian switched jackets; Athenaeum 1860 reburial).

**Ch XXII "Zuares and the Shark"**: Mutinous crew; Quail's log; Zuares kills shark in calm (rope round tail); Rose's diary; Dr Heriot. Ethel's locket (Morley's hair + miniature).

**Ch XXIII "Hawkshaw's Old Friends"**: Ethel forward tour (cat docked; scouse). Barradas threatens Hawkshaw; "Silenzio"; Hawkshaw's gold watch taken; crew throws dead body; the body's face looks like Morley.

**Ch XXIV "Up Anchor"**: Morley at Rio; letter posted for Ethel (never arrives). Princess chartered for Tasmania; Rio departure July 23; Hermione news; hermaphrodite brig near-collision; Noah.

**Ch XXV "The Suspicious Sail"**: Brigantine pursuing; Morrison's Hebridean bottle yarn; Coal-sack; flees; land appears; Morley & Tristan "Hermit" lead to next chapter.

**Ch XXVI "The Strange Island"**: Unknown island (not charted), goat-track, hut of hermit (Barradas), black-cock shot; ship's log. Hermit dies; Brother Pedro Zuares Miguel de Barradas, 1863. Burial; missal with confession found (Don Pedro Zuares Miguel de Barradas, Knight of Santiago).

**Ch XXVII "The Hermit"**: Missal confession: Don Pedro (Orizaba, Mariquita Escudero, son Juan Escudero killed by Pedro at San Juan de Ulloa; Pedro later threw overboard near Tristan; the Barradas brothers' birthmark cross on left shoulder). Princess sails on to Tristan d'Acunha; Morley to be "landed"; ends with Princess sailing south.

## VOL. II (Chapters I–XXV)
**Ch I "Mariquita Escudero"** (Pedro's confession, long): Pedro's seduction of Mariquita (daughter of Miguel Escudero, grangero of Orizaba); son Pedro born; second son Zuares; Miguel died; brother Juan Escudero duelled by Pedro on ramparts; Pedro sent to Spain, fell overboard; hencoop rescue; hermit. Princess reaches Tristan; Hermione's whereabouts later.

**Ch II "The Crew of the Hermione Discontented"**: Hawkshaw's guilt; Hermione passes Cape; Ethel and Manfredi (Promessi Sposi); Samuel Sharkey insults Ethel; Manfredi strikes him with marlinespike.

**Ch III "Rose and Dr. Heriot"**: Rose and Heriot on deck; engagement; ring (mother's).

**Ch IV "Man Overboard"**: Storm; Manfredi goes overboard (Joe the steward & Pedro); Sharkey suspected.

**Ch V "The Livid Face"**: Dana quotation; face at cabin window; Ethel and Rose terrified.

**Ch VI "What the Doctor Overheard in the Forecastle Bunks"**: Heriot eavesdrops; mutineers plan to take ship, walk plank, keep women, Calabar beans, Zuares: "Paso a paso."

**Ch VII "Measures for Defence Concerted"**: Council: seven men; arms; trunk barricade of law-books; Basset's watch.

**Ch VIII "The Sail to Windward"**: Princess (Bartelot, Morley as sailor; Noah's tattoo); Gough's Island; dismasted Princess; Morley's "pilgrim." Strange sail sighted.

**Ch IX "The Storm"**: Cape storm; Princess dismasted; Erwin lost; Plank lost.

**Ch X "The Four Castaways"**: Morley, Bartelot, Morrison, Noah on taffrail raft; Prussian barque *Einicheit* of Dantzic refuses rescue; Morley delirious.

**Ch XI "Captain Hawkshaw Makes a Discovery to Leeward"**: Hermione finds raft; Mr. Basset/Ethel conversation; albatross.

**Ch XII "Dr. Heriot's Patients"**: Four men rescued; name "Princess" read off wreck; Heriot's notes.

**Ch XIII "Captain Hawkshaw's Troubles Increase"**: Hawkshaw sees Morley among rescued men; plots murder.

**Ch XIV "Hawkshaw Turns Nurse"**: Hawkshaw volunteers night watch; Heriot gives poncho.

**Ch XV "A Biter Bitten"**: Hawkshaw attempts strangling Morley; Noah bites his hand.

**Ch XVI "Dread"**: Hawkshaw's lie; Basset; Ethel touches Hawkshaw's hand.

**Ch XVII "Unmasked"**: Morley reunited with Basset; Hawkshaw's crimes exposed; Morley's account of Acton Chine. Morrison's corpse-light story (Hester Udny & Willie).

**Ch XVIII "The Expulsion"**: Hawkshaw exiled to between-decks; Captain Phillips. Hawkshaw sends for Pedro's revenge.

**Ch XIX "The Meeting"**: Morley & Ethel reunited; Rose with Heriot; Noah Gawthrop; Heriot's Acton-Rennel.

**Ch XX "The Corpse-Licht"**: Morrison's Hester Udny tale (stowaway skeleton in Hobart Town hold).

**Ch XXI "Out of Scylla and into Charybdis"**: Quaco reveals Pedro's plot; Hawkshaw joins Pedro; "Sail to Cape."

**Ch XXII "Four Bells in the Dog-Watch"**: Mutiny begins; Hawkshaw in fore-cabin; girls' lots.

**Ch XXIII "The Crisis at Last"**: Morrison strikes Badger; mutiny; battle on deck.

**Ch XXIV "How the Ship Broached To"**: Mutiny; Joe killed by Pedro; Quail killed by nail-shot; Foster wounded.

**Ch XXV "The Cabin Attacked"**: Carronade fired at cabin; Quaco fires gun; Heriot's buck-shot; Quail's body thrown overboard.

## VOL. III (Chapters I–XXV)
**Ch I "Sail Ho!"**: Mutineers steer for Madagascar; scuttle-butt captured; Clyde (HMS, Captain Sir Horace Seymour) hails "General Jackson"; Pedro lies; Hawkshaw attacked by Pedro.

**Ch II "The Fortitude of Ethel"**: Ethel reads Revelation 21; Ethel abducted.

**Ch III "The Door in the Bulkhead"**: Pedro uses slide-door from steerage to girls' cabin; abducts Ethel.

**Ch IV "Ethel among the Mutineers"**: Hawkshaw kills Pedro with pistol; Hawkshaw rescues Ethel; Hawkshaw butchered by mutineers.

**Ch V "A Snare Laid"**: Ethel's hysteria; Pedro's arm shattered (Heriot); Hawkshaw dead.

**Ch VI "Mr. Basset Deluded"**: Bolter (Canadian) demands Basset parley; drugged brandy; Basset hanged at yard-arm.

**Ch VII "Lux Venit ab Alto"**: Heriot resuscitates Basset via tracheotomy/transfusion; "Lux venit ab alto."

**Ch VIII "The Valley of the Shadow"**: Basset recovering; Ethel nurses him.

**Ch IX "The Quarter-boat and its Freight"**: Mutineers set adrift in quarter-boat; Pedro dying.

**Ch X "Pedro's Wound"**: Heriot amputates Pedro's arm; Pedro's mother Mariquita.

**Ch XI "Remorse"**: Pedro confesses; Ethel reads him Bible; Pedro's last prayer.

**Ch XII "Story of a Modern Spanish Rogue"**: Pedro's story: Matriz Church; Ignez Moreno; St Peter; Orizaba image theft.

**Ch XIII "Ignez de Moreno"**: Pedro saves Ignez from water (Valparaiso); Don Salvador Moreno; Perez.

**Ch XIV "How Pedro provided Himself with a Horse and Valet"**: Pedro steals Hawkshaw's horse, Zuares as valet.

**Ch XV "The Alameda de la Canada"**: Pedro & Zuares in Santiago; Ignez; Perez; "Donna Erminia," "Donna Paula."

**Ch XVI "The Dressing-closet of Ignez"**: Pedro in closet; Perez discovers, drops Pedro from balcony.

**Ch XVII "The Great Crime of Pedro Barradas"**: Pedro sets fire to Church of La Campagnia (Dec 8); ~2000–3000 die; Ignez & Perez die.

**Ch XVIII "Committed to the Deep"**: Pedro dies (Madonna vision); buried at sea. Captain Phillips; Ethel & Rose.

**Ch XIX "Dr. Heriot's Fee"**: Basset's recovery; Rose & Heriot engagement; Cape Corrientes.

**Ch XX "Radama Puffadder"**: Malay trader Puffadder lures Hermione into mangrove creek; three red proas attack; Duke of Rothesay (Captain Duncan Davidson, Alloa) arrives.

**Ch XXI "The Mangrove Creek"**: Hermione's guns; Heriot, Morley spot proas; battle.

**Ch XXII "Eight Against Eighty"**: Hermione attacked; Morley's double-barrel broken; Noah's cheeks wounded by arrow; rescuers arrive.

**Ch XXIII "We'll Go to Sea No More"**: Duke of Rothesay saves Hermione; Scots song.

**Ch XXIV "The Anchor is let go"**: Arrival at Port Louis (Isle of France); Basset's daughters inherit £3000/yr each; Hermione sails on to Singapore with Heriot, Morrison, Foster. Noah joins HMS Clyde; mutineers Zuares & Badger dead in boat; Pedro's grave at Tristan.

**Ch XXV "Conclusion"**: Eight months later at Laurel Lodge: Ethel & Morley married (4 months); Rose & Heriot married; Heriot doctor at Acton-Kennel; Basset's gray hair; Phillips to marry Gravesend widow; Morrison in Scotland; Tom Bartelot to London; Noah Gawthrop at Basset Arms; Jack Page; Lucy Page; the squire. "THE END."
